# Design decisions

What was chosen, why, and what was rejected — split so that the design as it was
*planned* stays separable from what the build then found out.

- **[00 — initial decisions](00-initial-decisions.md)** is the whole design as it
  stood before the first ticket was picked up: §1–§31, settled in a grilling
  session on 2026-09-05. It is a fixed point, not a living document.
- **One file per ticket**, holding only what that ticket settled, corrected or
  contradicted. A ticket that changed nothing about the design has no file.

So a section of §1–§31 tells you what was intended, and the tickets listed
against it tell you what happened. Neither file rewrites the other.

Deferrals live in [../deferred.md](../deferred.md); the one decision that shapes
all the others is [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-asynchronous-transfer-lifecycle.md);
domain vocabulary is in [CONTEXT.md](../../CONTEXT.md). The tickets themselves
are in [`.scratch/global-payment-service/issues/`](../../.scratch/global-payment-service/issues/).

## Ticket records

| Ticket | What it settled |
|---|---|
| [01 — project skeleton](01-project-skeleton.md) | both Spring Boot 4 ecosystem bets won; what `@Enumerated(STRING)` actually emits; Boot 4's moved test furniture |
| [02 — Flyway wiring](02-flyway-wiring.md) | `spring-boot-flyway`, not `flyway-core` — the coordinate that silently runs nothing |
| [03 — package skeleton and ArchUnit](03-package-skeleton-archunit.md) | why an ArchUnit rule that matches nothing needs its own violation fixtures |
| [04 — security chain and CORS](04-security-chain-cors.md) | deny-by-default, and three rejected alternatives |
| [05 — problem detail contract](05-problem-detail-contract.md) | why `spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled` is absent; URN chosen from status, not exception |
| [06 — money and currency](06-money-and-currency.md) | `Money`'s four-method surface; two corrections to §29's mapping assumptions |
| [07 — the conversion function](07-conversion-function.md) | round-to-zero as a sealed outcome, not an empty `Optional`; why it lives in `fx`; the rate guard the shape needed |
| [08 — the Account entity](08-account-entity.md) | the identifier no section had chosen; why a `record` entity boots and then fails; two invariants in the table |
| [09 — creating an Account](09-create-account-endpoint.md) | why a typed `Currency` forced ticket 05's contract to widen; the Jackson default that truncates 100.50 into 100 |
| [10 — listing Accounts, and seed data](10-list-accounts-and-seed.md) | the service §30's tree omits and its own rule requires; two slice tests that assumed an empty scan root |
| [11 — the Transfer entity](11-transfer-entity.md) | `in (…)` in a check constraint is broken on H2; Accounts by ID rather than by association; one timestamp, not two |
| [12 — ordered Account locking](12-ordered-account-locking.md) | why two locking statements rather than one ordered query; which half of §6 each test can prove; why the locked-path rule's origin is a list and not a query over callers |
| [31 — frontend toolchain and shell](31-frontend-toolchain.md) | the generated route tree is committed *and* regenerated by the build; the SSE trap measured and named as gzip; `strict` is no longer in the Vite template |
| [32 — generated API types](32-openapi-type-generation.md) | springdoc publishes an API that never fails and whose responses are all optional — both closed on the backend; `nullable: true` is inert in OpenAPI 3.1; this generated file's diff is deliberately *not* hidden |

# Design decisions

What was chosen, why, and what was rejected — split so that the design as it was
*planned* stays separable from what the build then found out.

- **[00 — initial decisions](00-initial-decisions.md)** is the whole design as it
  stood before the first ticket was picked up: §1–§31, settled in a grilling
  session on 2026-09-05. It is a fixed point, not a living document.
- **One file per ticket**, holding only what that ticket settled, corrected or
  contradicted. A ticket that changed nothing about the design has no file.

So a section of §1–§31 tells you what was intended, and the tickets listed
against it tell you what happened. Neither file rewrites the other.

Deferrals live in [../deferred.md](../deferred.md); the one decision that shapes
all the others is [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-asynchronous-transfer-lifecycle.md);
domain vocabulary is in [CONTEXT.md](../../CONTEXT.md). The tickets themselves
are in [`.scratch/global-payment-service/issues/`](../../.scratch/global-payment-service/issues/).

## Ticket records

| Ticket | What it settled |
|---|---|
| [01 — project skeleton](01-project-skeleton.md) | both Spring Boot 4 ecosystem bets won; what `@Enumerated(STRING)` actually emits; Boot 4's moved test furniture |
| [02 — Flyway wiring](02-flyway-wiring.md) | `spring-boot-flyway`, not `flyway-core` — the coordinate that silently runs nothing |
| [03 — package skeleton and ArchUnit](03-package-skeleton-archunit.md) | why an ArchUnit rule that matches nothing needs its own violation fixtures |
| [04 — security chain and CORS](04-security-chain-cors.md) | deny-by-default, and three rejected alternatives |
| [05 — problem detail contract](05-problem-detail-contract.md) | why `spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled` is absent; URN chosen from status, not exception |
| [06 — money and currency](06-money-and-currency.md) | `Money`'s four-method surface; two corrections to §29's mapping assumptions |
| [07 — the conversion function](07-conversion-function.md) | round-to-zero as a sealed outcome, not an empty `Optional`; why it lives in `fx`; the rate guard the shape needed |
| [08 — the Account entity](08-account-entity.md) | the identifier no section had chosen; why a `record` entity boots and then fails; two invariants in the table |
| [09 — creating an Account](09-create-account-endpoint.md) | why a typed `Currency` forced ticket 05's contract to widen; the Jackson default that truncates 100.50 into 100 |
| [10 — listing Accounts, and seed data](10-list-accounts-and-seed.md) | the service §30's tree omits and its own rule requires; two slice tests that assumed an empty scan root |
| [11 — the Transfer entity](11-transfer-entity.md) | `in (…)` in a check constraint is broken on H2; Accounts by ID rather than by association; one timestamp, not two |
| [12 — ordered Account locking](12-ordered-account-locking.md) | why two locking statements rather than one ordered query; which half of §6 each test can prove; why the locked-path rule's origin is a list and not a query over callers |
| [31 — frontend toolchain and shell](31-frontend-toolchain.md) | the generated route tree is committed *and* regenerated by the build; the SSE trap measured and named as gzip; `strict` is no longer in the Vite template |
| [32 — generated API types](32-openapi-type-generation.md) | springdoc publishes an API that never fails and whose responses are all optional — both closed on the backend; `nullable: true` is inert in OpenAPI 3.1; this generated file's diff is deliberately *not* hidden |

# 32: Frontend types generated from the backend's OpenAPI document

**What to build:** A build step that generates the frontend's API types from the OpenAPI
document the backend serves, and a checked-in generated file the app imports from.

This is not a convenience. It is the only thing standing between the frontend test suite
and self-congratulation. The browser tests mock the network, so without generated types
they prove the frontend handles shapes **the test author invented**. With them, a mock
returning a shape the backend no longer produces is a failed build rather than a green
test.

It also puts the problem-type URNs in exactly one place, shared by both runtimes.

**The named risk, recorded rather than solved:** the generated file can go stale if nobody
regenerates it. Make regeneration a documented command, and treat a diff in the generated
file as a signal worth reading, not noise to commit past.

Base directory for this skill: /home/mherczeg/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).
- The brief: "Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

# Handoff — ticket 32 review fixes

**Task for this session:** apply the code-review fixes to the ticket 32 work, *including*
deciding the judgement calls. The feature itself is built, green, and reviewed; nothing
below is new feature work.

## Where the work is

- **Worktree:** `/data/mherczeg/projects/bankmonitor/.claude/worktrees/openapi-types`
  (branch `issue-32-openapi-types`, branched from `master` @ `f69e1e7`).
- **Nothing is committed.** All changes are in the working tree; untracked files were
  `git add -N`'d so `/usr/bin/git diff HEAD` shows the whole change.
- The previous session was told to pause before committing. **Ask before committing** unless
  the user has since said otherwise.

## What is already done (do not re-derive)

- The ticket and its acceptance criteria: `.scratch/global-payment-service/issues/32-openapi-type-generation.md`
  (all five ticked; the spec reviewer confirmed each tick is earned).
- Every design decision, rejected alternative and measured fact:
  `docs/design-decisions/32-openapi-type-generation.md`. **Read this first** — it explains
  why the backend changed at all, which is not obvious from the ticket.
- The diff: `/usr/bin/git diff HEAD` in the worktree.

Green as of the pause: backend `./mvnw -o test` → 111 tests; `cd frontend && npm run build`
→ clean; `npx vitest run` → 11; `npx oxlint` → clean.

## The fixes, in the order they should be made

Items 1–2 are placement mistakes made while editing. Items 3–5 came from the spec axis.
Items 6–10 are the judgement calls, each with the call already made — apply it, don't
re-litigate unless you find it wrong.

### 1. Orphaned Javadoc (hard)

`src/test/java/hu/bankmonitor/payments/accounts/AccountSchemaReachesTheDocumentTest.java:45`
— the new test was inserted between an existing Javadoc block and the method it documented.
Two Javadoc blocks now stack on `publishesEveryResponseMemberAsRequired()`, and
`publishesTheConstraintsOnTheRequest()` has none. Move the "ticket 39's form" block back
down onto `publishesTheConstraintsOnTheRequest`.

### 2. README section boundary (hard)

`frontend/README.md:57` — the new `## The API types, and when to regenerate them` heading
was inserted mid-section, so the pre-existing query-client, retry-rule, Bootstrap and
dev-proxy paragraphs now sit under it instead of under `## How it is put together`. Move the
new section to after the dev-proxy paragraph, at the end of the file.

### 3. `linguist-generated` is inverted (the ticket's named risk)

`frontend/.gitattributes` marks `src/api/schema.gen.ts` `linguist-generated=true` and four
documents claim this "leaves its diff visible". It does the opposite on the surface that
matters: `linguist-generated=true` is what collapses a file in a GitHub pull-request diff;
`-diff` only affects local `git diff`. The ticket's named risk is *"treat a diff in the
generated file as a signal worth reading, not noise to commit past"*, so this defeats the
one mitigation asked for.

**Fix:** change the entry to `src/api/schema.gen.ts -linguist-generated`, so the decision is
recorded rather than left to an absent line, and rewrite the comment above it. Then correct
the claim everywhere it appears — it currently says "marks the file generated but
deliberately leaves its diff visible" or similar in: `frontend/.gitattributes`,
`frontend/README.md`, `README.md`, `docs/deferred.md`,
`docs/design-decisions/32-openapi-type-generation.md` (§ "`schema.gen.ts` is committed, and
its diff is left visible"). Grep for `-diff` and `linguist` to find them all.

### 4. `instance` should be required

`src/main/java/hu/bankmonitor/payments/OpenApiConfiguration.java` marks only
`type, title, status, detail` required. Spring populates `instance` on every problem
document — `src/test/java/hu/bankmonitor/payments/ProblemDocumentContractTest.java:177`
asserts it — so a mock omitting it compiles, which is the same hole the `AccountResponse`
`required` work exists to close.

This one has a tail; all of it must move together:

- `OpenApiConfiguration.problemDocument()` — add `"instance"` to `setRequired(...)`, and fix
  the Javadoc above it that names which members are optional.
- `ProblemSchemaReachesTheDocumentTest.namesTheEnumerationOnTheTypeMember()` — its
  `containsExactlyInAnyOrder("type", "title", "status", "detail")` must gain `"instance"`.
- **Regenerate `frontend/src/api/schema.gen.ts`** (see *Regenerating* below) — `instance`
  moves from `instance?: string` to `instance: string`.
- `frontend/src/api/types.test.ts` — the `aProblem` fixture has no `instance` and will stop
  compiling. Add one, e.g. `instance: '/api/accounts'`.

### 5. Factual slip

`docs/design-decisions/32-openapi-type-generation.md:19` says "the nine problem-type URNs".
`ProblemType` has ten constants.

### 6. Judgement call — `.gitattributes` comment length → **trim**

Three lines restating the design record, where `AGENTS.md` (*Code style*, configuration-file
exception) allows "a short line of intent per non-obvious key". Cut to one or two lines
naming the decision; the reasoning already lives in the design record and both READMEs.
Fold this into fix 3, since that rewrites the comment anyway.

### 7. Judgement call — duplicated prose across the two READMEs → **split by audience, keep both**

The same argument appears in near-identical prose in `README.md` (the new "The frontend's
types are generated, not written" section) and `frontend/README.md`. `AGENTS.md` is explicit
that a surviving document must stand on its own and must *not* be trimmed to a pointer — so
do not delete either. Split them instead:

- **Root `README.md` owns the argument**: why the document had to be fixed on the backend
  first (the two gaps and their table), why the output is committed, what the trade costs.
- **`frontend/README.md` owns the operation**: the command, when to run it, read the diff,
  where the residual risk is written up. Cut its restatement of the four drifted shapes and
  of the `.gitattributes` reasoning down to a sentence, and point at the root README's
  section for the why.

### 8. Judgement call — duplicated problem-document member names → **share the one name this codebase invented, leave the RFC's**

`OpenApiConfiguration.problemDocument()` writes `"type"`, `"title"`, `"status"`, `"detail"`,
`"instance"`, `"errors"` as literals; `ProblemDocumentAdvice` holds
`private static final String VALIDATION_ERRORS = "errors"`.

- `type/title/status/detail/instance` are **RFC 9457's vocabulary, not this codebase's** —
  they cannot be renamed here, so a shared constant would buy nothing. Leave them, and say
  so in a short comment.
- `errors` **is** this codebase's invention and exists twice. Widen
  `ProblemDocumentAdvice.VALIDATION_ERRORS` to package-private and reference it from
  `OpenApiConfiguration` (both classes are in `hu.bankmonitor.payments`).
- The restated required list in `ProblemSchemaReachesTheDocumentTest` **stays a literal**.
  That is the repo's stated position, not an oversight — see `AccountController`'s Javadoc:
  *"a test reading the same constant as the mapping would follow the rename silently instead
  of failing on it."*

### 9. Judgement call — unused exports in `types.ts` → **keep, and say why**

`NewAccount`, `Currency` and `ValidationError` are exported but imported nowhere yet. The
reviewer flagged Speculative Generality. **Push back:** these are not an abstraction built
for a hypothetical need — each is a one-line alias of a shape the backend already publishes,
and the module's whole job is to be the single place `schema.gen.ts` is read from. Tickets 34
(`ValidationError`, `ProblemType`) and 39/40 (`NewAccount`, `Currency`) are the named
consumers. Add a sentence to the module docstring saying the module mirrors the API's
published shapes rather than only what today's screens import, so the next reader does not
re-raise it.

### 10. Judgement calls — two small ones in the same files

- `frontend/src/api/types.test.ts` — `it('reaches the frontend as the closed set the backend
  declares')` has a vacuous runtime assertion (`expect(aProblem.type).not.toBe(reused)`).
  **Delete that test.** The one after it (`refuses a URN this API never emits`) already
  proves the closed set, and proves it the way the file's own docstring says it proves
  things.
- `OpenApiConfiguration.PROBLEM_MEDIA_TYPE` uses a fully-qualified
  `org.springframework.http.MediaType` to dodge a clash with the imported swagger
  `io.swagger.v3.oas.models.media.MediaType`. That is exactly `AGENTS.md`'s "a warning where
  the obvious edit is the wrong one" case — add the one-line comment.

## Environment gotchas found the hard way

- **Invoke git as `/usr/bin/git`.** A shell hook rewrites bare `git` to `rtk git`, which the
  worktree-isolation guard then refuses. Also: run git from the worktree root, not from
  `frontend/`.
- **Port 8080 is occupied by a foreign Spring instance** (not this worktree's, and running
  older code — do not kill it). Start this worktree's backend on 8081 instead:
  ```bash
  ./mvnw -o -q spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments=--server.port=8081
  ```
  Use Bash `run_in_background` for it; a `(cmd &)` subshell gets tangled with the tool's
  process handling. Poll with `curl` **and a `sleep`** — boot takes ~25s.
- **Regenerating** (needed after fix 4). The committed script points at 8080, which is
  correct for a normal machine; from here run it against 8081 by hand. The output is
  byte-identical either way — `openapi-typescript` does not emit `servers[]`:
  ```bash
  cd frontend && npx openapi-typescript http://localhost:8081/v3/api-docs --output src/api/schema.gen.ts
  ```
- **`openapi-typescript@7.13.0` declares `peerDependencies: { typescript: "^5.x" }`** and the
  repo is on TypeScript 6. Resolved by an `overrides` entry in `frontend/package.json` — do
  not remove it, and do not "fix" installs with `--legacy-peer-deps`.
- `npm run lint` prints a broken-JSON line through the rtk wrapper; run `npx oxlint` directly.

## Verifying when done

```bash
./mvnw -o test                                   # expect 111 tests, BUILD SUCCESS
cd frontend && npm run build && npx vitest run && npx oxlint
```

And re-prove the ticket's demonstration still bites, since fix 4 touches that file: delete
one `@ts-expect-error` from `frontend/src/api/types.test.ts`, confirm `npx tsc -b --force`
fails naming the case, then restore it.

## Suggested skills

- **`mattpocock-skills:code-review`** — re-run it after the fixes, same two axes, fixed point
  `HEAD` with untracked files `add -N`'d. Fixes 3, 4 and 7 all touch documents the first
  review read, so a second pass is worth its cost.
- **`land-worktree`** — only once the user has approved committing; it fast-forwards the
  branch onto `master` and removes the worktree.

Do **not** reach for `mattpocock-skills:tdd` or `implement` here; this is corrective editing
against a finished, reviewed change, and every fix has its test already written.

## User preferences that apply

- Explain Java- and Spring-specific decisions inline; the user does not work in Java.
- Ask design questions one at a time, with a visible queue. No time estimates.
- Self-documenting code; inline comments only for a non-obvious *why*, an outside-world fact,
  or a warning — see `AGENTS.md`.
- `docs/design-decisions/`, `docs/deferred.md` and `.scratch/` are disposable scaffolding;
  `README.md`, the READMEs beside the code, `CONTEXT.md` and Javadoc are what a maintainer
  inherits. When a fact belongs in both, the durable document gets the full statement.

down onto `publishesTheConstraintsOnTheRequest`.

### 2. README section boundary (hard)

`frontend/README.md:57` — the new `## The API types, and when to regenerate them` heading
was inserted mid-section, so the pre-existing query-client, retry-rule, Bootstrap and
dev-proxy paragraphs now sit under it instead of under `## How it is put together`. Move the
new section to after the dev-proxy paragraph, at the end of the file.

### 3. `linguist-generated` is inverted (the ticket's named risk)

`frontend/.gitattributes` marks `src/api/schema.gen.ts` `linguist-generated=true` and four
documents claim this "leaves its diff visible". It does the opposite on the surface that
matters: `linguist-generated=true` is what collapses a file in a GitHub pull-request diff;
`-diff` only affects local `git diff`. The ticket's named risk is *"treat a diff in the
generated file as a signal worth reading, not noise to commit past"*, so this defeats the
one mitigation asked for.

**Fix:** change the entry to `src/api/schema.gen.ts -linguist-generated`, so the decision is
recorded rather than left to an absent line, and rewrite the comment above it. Then correct
the claim everywhere it appears — it currently says "marks the file generated but
deliberately leaves its diff visible" or similar in: `frontend/.gitattributes`,
`frontend/README.md`, `README.md`, `docs/deferred.md`,
`docs/design-decisions/32-openapi-type-generation.md` (§ "`schema.gen.ts` is committed, and
its diff is left visible"). Grep for `-diff` and `linguist` to find them all.

### 4. `instance` should be required

`src/main/java/hu/bankmonitor/payments/OpenApiConfiguration.java` marks only
`type, title, status, detail` required. Spring populates `instance` on every problem
document — `src/test/java/hu/bankmonitor/payments/ProblemDocumentContractTest.java:177`
asserts it — so a mock omitting it compiles, which is the same hole the `AccountResponse`
`required` work exists to close.

This one has a tail; all of it must move together:

- `OpenApiConfiguration.problemDocument()` — add `"instance"` to `setRequired(...)`, and fix
  the Javadoc above it that names which members are optional.
- `ProblemSchemaReachesTheDocumentTest.namesTheEnumerationOnTheTypeMember()` — its
  `containsExactlyInAnyOrder("type", "title", "status", "detail")` must gain `"instance"`.
- **Regenerate `frontend/src/api/schema.gen.ts`** (see *Regenerating* below) — `instance`
  moves from `instance?: string` to `instance: string`.
- `frontend/src/api/types.test.ts` — the `aProblem` fixture has no `instance` and will stop
  compiling. Add one, e.g. `instance: '/api/accounts'`.

### 5. Factual slip

`docs/design-decisions/32-openapi-type-generation.md:19` says "the nine problem-type URNs".
`ProblemType` has ten constants.

### 6. Judgement call — `.gitattributes` comment length → **trim**

Three lines restating the design record, where `AGENTS.md` (*Code style*, configuration-file
exception) allows "a short line of intent per non-obvious key". Cut to one or two lines
naming the decision; the reasoning already lives in the design record and both READMEs.
Fold this into fix 3, since that rewrites the comment anyway.

### 7. Judgement call — duplicated prose across the two READMEs → **split by audience, keep both**

The same argument appears in near-identical prose in `README.md` (the new "The frontend's
types are generated, not written" section) and `frontend/README.md`. `AGENTS.md` is explicit
that a surviving document must stand on its own and must *not* be trimmed to a pointer — so
do not delete either. Split them instead:

- **Root `README.md` owns the argument**: why the document had to be fixed on the backend
  first (the two gaps and their table), why the output is committed, what the trade costs.
- **`frontend/README.md` owns the operation**: the command, when to run it, read the diff,
  where the residual risk is written up. Cut its restatement of the four drifted shapes and
  of the `.gitattributes` reasoning down to a sentence, and point at the root README's
  section for the why.

### 8. Judgement call — duplicated problem-document member names → **share the one name this codebase invented, leave the RFC's**

`OpenApiConfiguration.problemDocument()` writes `"type"`, `"title"`, `"status"`, `"detail"`,
`"instance"`, `"errors"` as literals; `ProblemDocumentAdvice` holds
`private static final String VALIDATION_ERRORS = "errors"`.

- `type/title/status/detail/instance` are **RFC 9457's vocabulary, not this codebase's** —
  they cannot be renamed here, so a shared constant would buy nothing. Leave them, and say
  so in a short comment.
- `errors` **is** this codebase's invention and exists twice. Widen
  `ProblemDocumentAdvice.VALIDATION_ERRORS` to package-private and reference it from
  `OpenApiConfiguration` (both classes are in `hu.bankmonitor.payments`).
- The restated required list in `ProblemSchemaReachesTheDocumentTest` **stays a literal**.
  That is the repo's stated position, not an oversight — see `AccountController`'s Javadoc:
  *"a test reading the same constant as the mapping would follow the rename silently instead
  of failing on it."*

### 9. Judgement call — unused exports in `types.ts` → **keep, and say why**

`NewAccount`, `Currency` and `ValidationError` are exported but imported nowhere yet. The
reviewer flagged Speculative Generality. **Push back:** these are not an abstraction built
for a hypothetical need — each is a one-line alias of a shape the backend already publishes,
and the module's whole job is to be the single place `schema.gen.ts` is read from. Tickets 34
(`ValidationError`, `ProblemType`) and 39/40 (`NewAccount`, `Currency`) are the named
consumers. Add a sentence to the module docstring saying the module mirrors the API's
published shapes rather than only what today's screens import, so the next reader does not
re-raise it.

### 10. Judgement calls — two small ones in the same files

- `frontend/src/api/types.test.ts` — `it('reaches the frontend as the closed set the backend
  declares')` has a vacuous runtime assertion (`expect(aProblem.type).not.toBe(reused)`).
  **Delete that test.** The one after it (`refuses a URN this API never emits`) already
  proves the closed set, and proves it the way the file's own docstring says it proves
  things.
- `OpenApiConfiguration.PROBLEM_MEDIA_TYPE` uses a fully-qualified
  `org.springframework.http.MediaType` to dodge a clash with the imported swagger
  `io.swagger.v3.oas.models.media.MediaType`. That is exactly `AGENTS.md`'s "a warning where
  the obvious edit is the wrong one" case — add the one-line comment.

- **Invoke git as `/usr/bin/git`.** A shell hook rewrites bare `git` to `rtk git`, which the
